sentences.text: Huaxiagnathus is an extinct coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China.
The largest known specimen is about 1.8 meters in length, making it one of the largest compsognathids, longer than Compsognathus and the largest Sinosauropteryx specimens.

It is distinguished from other compsognathids by a long premaxillary process overlapping the antorbital fossa, a hand as long as the combined humerus and radius, large first and second claws 167% the length of the third claw, a first metacarpal narrower than the second, and a reduced olecranon process.

The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was collected from the Yixian Formation at Dabangou Village near Beipiao City in western Liaoning Province, dating to 125 million years ago.
Cladistic analysis places Huaxiagnathus at the base of Compsognathidae due to its unspecialized arms.

Huaxiagnathus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia. The time range for Huaxiagnathus is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
A 2024 study by Andrea Cau questioned whether Huaxiagnathus belongs within Compsognathidae, noting it was known only from immature specimens.
Cau and Paterna (2025) proposed that Sinotyrannus is a mature form of Huaxiagnathus, suggesting the name Huaxiagnathus has priority.
